title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Todays Value And The World Lit By Prayer

questions.question: What does the passage say about yesterday and tomorrow?
questions.answer: Yesterday is gone, and tomorrow is not promised to us.

questions.question: According to the passage, which time is your real life right now?
questions.answer: The present day.

questions.question: What should a person do with at least one hour of the day?
questions.answer: Spend it in prayer and worship.

questions.question: How is that hour of worship described for the hereafter?
questions.answer: It is like saving something valuable for the real future.

questions.question: What is each new day compared to for every person?
questions.answer: A doorway to a new personal world.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s daily world if the prayers are not performed?
questions.answer: It becomes dark and miserable and stands against the person.

questions.question: What shapes a person’s private world each day?
questions.answer: The person’s heart, thoughts, actions, and wishes.

questions.question: Why does the passage use the example of a mirror and a palace?
questions.answer: To show that the same thing can look beautiful or ugly depending on what reflects it, just as a person’s inner state changes his daily world.

questions.question: What change happens when someone performs the five daily prayers sincerely?
questions.answer: That person’s world becomes bright because he turns toward Allah.

questions.question: What example is used to explain how prayer brings light?
questions.answer: Prayer is compared to turning on a lamp with a switch.

questions.question: What do the prayers help a person see in the world’s confusion?
questions.answer: They help the person see wisdom, order, and meaning.

questions.question: What effect does this light have on the person’s world that day?
questions.answer: It makes that world shine and speak in the person’s favor.

questions.question: What warning is given about thinking, “My prayers are too small”?
questions.answer: A small prayer still carries the same basic truth, just like a seed carries the pattern of the tree.

questions.question: How are the prayers of ordinary people and great saints alike?
questions.answer: Both share in the same light, even if not at the same level.

questions.question: What is different between the prayers of different people?
questions.answer: Their depth, brightness, and level are different.

questions.question: What stays present in all levels of prayer?
questions.answer: The core of that blessed light remains in every level.

questions.question: Why does the passage tell the nafs not to count on tomorrow?
questions.answer: Because no one has proof that tomorrow will come for him.

questions.question: What wise choice does the passage ask a person to make today?
questions.answer: To give at least one hour to prayer and worship.

questions.question: Why is that one hour a smart use of time?
questions.answer: Because it is stored like savings for the life to come.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about each day in a person’s life?
questions.answer: Each day brings a new world for that person.

questions.question: If someone ignores prayer during the day, how will that day’s world end?
questions.answer: It will leave in a sad and dark condition and become a witness against that person.

questions.question: In this passage, what decides whether a person’s daily world is bright or dark?
questions.answer: The condition of the person’s heart and the way he lives and acts.

questions.question: How does the mirror example help explain this idea?
questions.answer: It shows that what is inside and around the reflection changes how the picture appears.

questions.question: What can a person do to his own world by his choices?
questions.answer: He can make it support him or speak against him.

questions.question: What is one result of performing the five daily prayers?
questions.answer: A person turns toward the Creator of that world.

questions.question: What happens right away to the person’s world after that turning?
questions.answer: It becomes filled with light.

questions.question: What does prayer uncover in the middle of life’s mess and confusion?
questions.answer: It uncovers a planned and meaningful order.

questions.question: How does the verse about Allah being the Light connect to the person’s day?
questions.answer: Its light reaches the heart and brightens that person’s world.

questions.question: What does the passage say that bright world will do for the person?
questions.answer: It will testify for the person, not against him.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain even a small prayer?
questions.answer: A seed and the full tree it can grow into.

questions.question: What does that comparison teach about ordinary people’s prayers?
questions.answer: Even simple prayers hold a real share of the same truth and light.

questions.question: Why are some prayers stronger or brighter than others?
questions.answer: Because people differ in spiritual level and in how much that truth opens in them.

questions.question: What should a person understand about time from this passage?
questions.answer: The past is over, the future is uncertain, and today is what we truly have.

questions.question: What does the passage encourage a Muslim to do with part of today?
questions.answer: Use at least one hour for salah and worship.

questions.question: What picture is given to show the value of that hour?
questions.answer: It is like putting treasure aside for the hereafter.

questions.question: What special meaning does each new day have?
questions.answer: It opens a fresh personal world.

questions.question: According to the passage, can two people’s daily worlds be the same in quality?
questions.answer: No, because each one depends on that person’s inner state and deeds.

questions.question: What makes a daily world become sad and dark?
questions.answer: Leaving the prayers undone.

questions.question: In what way can a day become a witness?
questions.answer: It can either support the person or stand as evidence against him.

questions.question: What four things are named as shaping a person’s world?
questions.answer: The heart, the mind, the actions, and the wishes.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of a smooth or rough mirror?
questions.answer: A person’s condition affects how his world appears, just as a mirror changes a reflection.

questions.question: What is the first big effect of the five daily prayers on a person’s world?
questions.answer: They bring brightness by connecting the person to Allah.

questions.question: Why are prayers compared to switching on a lamp?
questions.answer: Because they drive away darkness and help a person see clearly.

questions.question: After that light comes, how does the world look different?
questions.answer: It no longer seems meaningless and confused but full of wisdom and purpose.

questions.question: What should a person not say about his own prayers?
questions.answer: He should not think they are worthless compared with greater prayers.

questions.question: How does the date seed example answer that wrong thought?
questions.answer: It shows that a small beginning still carries the truth of what it can become.

questions.question: What do both a saint’s prayer and an ordinary Muslim’s prayer share?
questions.answer: Both have a portion of the same spiritual light.

questions.question: What varies among people’s prayers while the core stays the same?
questions.answer: Their stages, strength, and degree of unfolding vary, but the essence remains.

questions.question: What is the main message about how to view the day you are living in?
questions.answer: Treat today as your real chance, since the past is gone and the future is not guaranteed.

questions.question: What does the passage ask you to do with one hour of the day?
questions.answer: Dedicate it to worship.

questions.question: Why is worship in that hour compared to keeping something in a safe place?
questions.answer: Because it is being saved for the everlasting life ahead.

questions.question: What does every new day open for a person?
questions.answer: A new world that belongs to that day.

questions.question: If a person leaves prayer, what kind of world does that day become for him?
questions.answer: A gloomy and unhappy one.

questions.question: Where will that dark daily world speak against the person?
questions.answer: In the unseen realm mentioned in the passage.

questions.question: What decides the condition of a person’s daily world?
questions.answer: His inner life and what he does.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention mirrors of different colors and qualities?
questions.answer: To explain that the same reality can look different depending on the one reflecting it.

questions.question: How can a person change the look of his own world?
questions.answer: By what he loves, thinks, intends, and does.

questions.question: What happens when someone keeps the five daily prayers?
questions.answer: He turns toward the Creator, and his world becomes bright.

questions.question: What does prayer remove from the person’s world?
questions.answer: Darkness and the feeling of miserable confusion.

questions.question: What does prayer reveal instead of chaos?
questions.answer: Order, wisdom, and meaningful signs of Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the light mentioned in the passage reach the person?
questions.answer: It reflects onto the heart and lights up that day’s world.

questions.question: What result comes from that shining world?
questions.answer: It becomes a witness for the person.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage tell us to avoid about our own salah?
questions.answer: Thinking it has no real value because it is not like the prayer of very holy people.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the link between simple prayers and higher prayers?
questions.answer: They share the same root truth, even though some are much more developed than others.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about depending on tomorrow?
questions.answer: A person should not rely on tomorrow because it may never come.

questions.question: Since the future is uncertain, what should a person value most?
questions.answer: The day he is living right now.

questions.question: What simple act with time does the passage strongly encourage?
questions.answer: Giving at least one hour to prayer.

questions.question: How is that hour helpful for the life after death?
questions.answer: It is stored like savings for the true future.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying each day is the door to a new world?
questions.answer: Every day forms its own personal life record and condition for the person.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of not praying during the day?
questions.answer: The person’s day becomes spiritually dark.

questions.question: What further result comes from that darkness?
questions.answer: That day will later count against the person.

questions.question: What comparison shows how the heart affects a person’s world?
questions.answer: The comparison of a palace seen in different mirrors.

questions.question: If the “mirror” is bad, what happens to the reflected picture?
questions.answer: Even something beautiful can look ugly or rough.

questions.question: What does this teach about a person’s heart and actions?
questions.answer: They shape how his world appears and what kind of witness it becomes.

questions.question: What do the five daily prayers do to the person’s world?
questions.answer: They fill it with light.

questions.question: Why is the lamp image a good example for prayer?
questions.answer: Because prayer lights up what was dark and hidden.

questions.question: Once light comes, how does the world’s disorder look?
questions.answer: It appears as something arranged with wisdom and meaning.

questions.question: What should a regular person believe about his own prayer?
questions.answer: It still has a share in the same blessed light as the prayer of the righteous.

questions.question: What example explains this truth in a simple way?
questions.answer: A date seed that already contains the pattern of the tree.

questions.question: What stays the same in all true prayers, even when people are at different levels?
questions.answer: Their shining essence stays the same.

questions.question: What two facts about time are given at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The past has gone, and the future is not guaranteed.

questions.question: Based on those facts, what is called a person’s true life?
questions.answer: Today, the present day.

questions.question: What should be done with at least one hour of that day?
questions.answer: It should be used for worship, especially prayer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of spending that hour in worship?
questions.answer: To prepare for the hereafter.

questions.question: What new thing comes with each day for every person?
questions.answer: A new personal world.

questions.question: What makes that daily world leave in darkness and sadness?
questions.answer: Neglecting the prayers.

questions.question: Can that daily world affect a person later? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. It can later speak either for the person or against him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what helps build the condition of that world?
questions.answer: A person’s heart, mind, deeds, and desires.

questions.question: Why is the palace-and-mirror picture important in this passage?
questions.answer: It helps explain that our inner condition changes how our world is shown to us.

questions.question: What happens when a person performs the five daily prayers?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah, and his world lights up.

questions.question: What everyday object is used to explain this sudden brightness?
questions.answer: An electric light turned on by a switch.

questions.question: What does that light help the person understand about life?
questions.answer: That behind confusion there is divine wisdom and order.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this light to the heart?
questions.answer: The light falls on the heart and then brightens the person’s whole day.

questions.question: What good testimony comes from a brightened daily world?
questions.answer: It bears witness in the person’s favor.

questions.question: What example is given to show that even small prayers matter?
questions.answer: A date seed still belongs to the same reality as the full tree.

questions.question: What is the final lesson about different people’s prayers?
questions.answer: They are not equal in level, but all true prayers contain the same basic luminous truth.
